lines: Between the library and the ride, every class now has its Class Start.
From its card, the class opens with its channel, length and focus, its title and its summary. Classes leads back.
What the bike will do: thirty minutes, the resistance profile, and eight efforts with recoveries from three minutes down to ninety seconds.
The average is each segment's target power, weighted by how long it lasts. About one hundred and fifty four watts.
The class video waits, parked at its sync point with its controls showing, and goes when you leave.
Video link and sync opens to the class on YouTube, and the moment the ride syncs from.
How do you want to ride? Ride alone is chosen. Group sessions can't be reached yet, and the group option says so.
Start class goes straight into the class ride, alone, with the bike following the plan.
A locked class's address opens the library instead, as does a class the catalogue doesn't hold.
The same page, from one column on a phone to two on a desktop.
What the tests prove: seven behaviour specs and nine unit tests, all green, and the first bundle still under budget.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
